description.narrative:
Interpeace har ansökt om 77 miljoner SEK i stöd för att genomföra insatsen '’Reinforcing community capacity for social cohesion and reconciliation through Societal Trauma Healing in Rwanda’, 2021-2025, mellan juli 2021 till juni 2022. Insatsen genomförs i samarbete med Prison Fellowship Rwanda (RFP), Haguruka och Dignity in Detention Organisation (DiDe).
Insatsens mål syftar till att stärka den mentala hälsan hos de som drabbats av folkmordet mot Tutsierna 1994 och deras emotionella och finansiella resiliens och i längde verka för hållbar fred. Mer specifikt syftar insatsen på att stärka återintegreringen av fängelsfångar dömda för folkmordsbrott som kommer att släppas under de kommande fyra åren och minska risker relaterad till återintegreringen, såsom förväntade ökade fall av könsbaserat våld, spänningar, konflikter och ökade nivåer av trauma. Insatsen arbetar även mer Rwandas yngre befolkning för att minska intergenerationstrauma och därmed motverka radikalisering och ökade spänningar bland den yngre generationen. Programmet är uppdelat i fyra resultatområden med specifika mål och aktiviteter, (1) Förbättrad läkning och psykosocial motståndskraft bland män, kvinnor och unga i samhället och inom fängelser, (2) Förbättrad social sammanhållning och återintegrering av folkmordsdömda fängelsegångar (3) Inkluderande och kollektiva försörjningsmöjligheter för män, kvinnor och unga i samhället och fängelser för att förbättra välbefinnandet, social samanhållning och försoning, och (4) Stärkande av nationell policy och program inom ramen för helande, social sammanhållning och försoning, samt försörjningsmöjligheter för de fattigaste, inklusive släppta fängelsefångar och de som överlevde folkmordet mot Tutsierna.
Sverige står som enskild finansiär av insatsen men förhoppningen är antalet givare kommer att öka under insatsens gång vid en eventuell utökning av insatser till andra distrikt. CKCK MSK kommer vidareförmedlas till partnerorganisationer samt TVET-institutioner.

Interpeace has submitted to the Embassy a proposal for a four-year programme titled, ’Reinforcing community capacity for social cohesion and reconciliation through Societal Trauma Healing in Rwanda’. The proposed duration of the programme is July 2021 to June 2025, and the budget is 77 million SEK. The contribution will be implemented in close collaboration with Prison Fellowship Rwanda ( RFP), HAGURUKA and Dignity in Detention Organization (DiDe).
The proposed programme aims to address and heal the psycho-social wounds that has been caused by the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi and strengthen social cohesion, trust building and socio-economic development with the longer perspective of promoting sustainable peace in Rwanda. This will be achieved through trauma healing, community dialogue, and small-scale livelihood projects. A strong emphasis is put on the releases of prisoners convicted of crimes relating to the Genocide against the Tutsi and their reintegration back into their communities as well as on youth, and their ability to heal from inter-generational trauma. The program is divided into four result areas with specific goals and activities, (1) Improved healing and psychosocial resilience among men, women and young people in society and in prisons, (2) Improved social cohesion and reintegration of genocidal convictions (3) Inclusion and collective livelihoods for men, women and young people in society and prisons for the development of well-being, social cohesion and reconciliation; genocide survivor.
Sweden is the sole financier of the contribution, but there is an anticipation that additional donors will fund a potential up-scale of the programme. CKCK MSK will be passed on to partner organizations and TVET institutions.

The objective of the programme is to strengthen psychosocial and socioeconomic resilience for sustainable peace among communities in five districts in Rwanda through five outcomes:
Enhanced healing and psychosocial resilience among men, women, youth and other vulnerable groups in communities and prisons.
Enhanced social cohesion and prisoners psychosocial reintegration.
Improved socio-economic inclusion and collective livelihood opportunities for men, women, youth, and other vulnerable groups.
National policies and programmes on healing, social cohesion and collective livelihoods are informed by lessons learned from programme interventions.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
Objective 1: Enhanced healing and psychosocial resilience among men, women, and youth in communities and prisons in the five districts:
The programme achieved substantial improvements in participants mental health outcomes, with notable reductions across all measured conditions between the 2023 baseline and the 2025 endline. Post Traumatic Stress Disorder, anxiety, depression, and Borderline Personality Disorder showed significant declines, ranging from 40% to 47%, indicating strong effectiveness of the trauma healing and social cohesion interventions. Participants testimonies reinforced these findings, highlighting restored hope, improved emotional stability, and tangible behavior change, such as reduced suicidal ideation and healthier coping strategies. Although aggression decreased more modestly at 14.5%, the overall results demonstrate that the programme delivered meaningful psychosocial impact and exceeded several of its intended targets.
The programme achieved consistent and meaningful improvements across all psychosocial dimensions, with participants demonstrating increased resilience, stronger social cohesion, higher levels of hopefulness, and significant gains in emotional wellbeing. Notably, emotional wellbeing, collaboration, and self management recorded the largest improvements, reflecting enhanced emotional regulation, greater willingness to work collectively, and stronger personal discipline. These positive shifts indicate that the Resilience Oriented Therapy interventions did more than alleviate distress, they actively strengthened internal coping capacities and community based protective factors essential for long-term recovery. Overall, the results show that the programme effectively fostered healing, reconciliation, and psychological stability within trauma affected communities.
Outcome 2: Enhanced Social Cohesion and Prisoners' Psychosocial Reintegration
The Multifamily Healing Sessions (MFHS) produced substantial positive shifts in family functioning, with meaningful improvements observed in communication (13.5%), belief systems (11%), organizational patterns (9.7%), and nurturing parenting practices, including a notable rise in authoritative democratic parenting (12.6%). Modest yet important gains were also recorded in gender roles (3.6%) and intergenerational harmony (3.4%), although deeply rooted norms and longstanding family dynamics proved more resistant to change. The intervention surfaced reductions in authoritarian parenting (1.8%) and highlighted emerging awareness of power imbalances within intimate relationships, reflected in a decline in sexual relationship power (14.5%), underscoring the need for continued gender sensitive support. Overall, these results demonstrate that the MFHS model effectively strengthened communication, improved relational wellbeing, and fostered healthier, more resilient family dynamics, while also pointing to areas requiring deeper or longer-term engagement.
Sociotherapy in correctional facilities contributed meaningfully to strengthening social harmony among inmates and their families by fostering empathy, trust, and mutual respect through structured group dialogues and community oriented activities. These sessions helped reduce fear, discrimination, and social mistrust while reinforcing feelings of belonging, social support, and confidence in seeking help, thereby improving reintegration readiness and emotional healing. Improvements were observed even where baseline perceptions were already strong, such as maintaining good relationships across different family backgrounds, reflecting consolidation of positive attitudes rather than dramatic shifts. Testimonies from inmates and implementing partners further confirmed that sociotherapy encouraged behavior change, with participants becoming more disciplined, less judgmental, and more open to understanding others.
Outcome 3: Inclusive and Collaborative Livelihoods
The impact under this objective was mainly realized through inmates being prepared for reintegration into the society after serving their respective sentences.
The TVET programme produced a transformative shift in inmates vocational capacity, moving participants from overwhelmingly limited or no prior technical knowledge to 100% acquisition of at least one marketable skill. Significant growth was recorded across all trades, particularly hairdressing, sewing, and handcraft, demonstrating strong uptake and effective training across Musanze, Nyagatare, and Nyamagabe correctional facilities. This improvement not only enhanced inmates employability and self-reliance but also contributed to personal confidence, purposeful engagement, and readiness for social reintegration after release. Overall, the results show that TVET served as a powerful rehabilitative and economic empowerment tool, equipping inmates with practical skills and improving their prospects for successful reintegration into their families and communities.
The TVET programme generated multidimensional benefits for inmates, strengthening their psychological wellbeing, social connections, and readiness for economic reintegration. Inmates reported increased self-esteem, purposeful use of time, stronger social bonds, and opportunities for income earning activities, demonstrating how vocational training contributes to both rehabilitation and healthier correctional environments. After release, the acquired skills are expected to support easy entry into the job market, foster entrepreneurship, and enable former inmates to become productive family and community members. Overall, the results show that TVET is a powerful tool for reducing recidivism, enhancing dignity, and equipping inmates with the competencies needed to rebuild their lives and reintegrate successfully into society.
